## lib-email-provider

**One boundary** to fetch a Gmail **message** or **thread** *by reference*, search the mailbox (`list`), or report a message as spam (`report_spam`) — the single Gmail→other-provider swap point (one credential, one access point).

**Input** (Execute Sub-workflow):
- `mode`: message | thread | list | report_spam
- `source_ref`: { `uuid` (message id — message / report_spam), `conversation_id` (thread id — thread) } — ids must match `[A-Za-z0-9_-]+`
- `scope_query`: Gmail search string (list, non-empty)
- `include_attachments` / `max_attachment_bytes`: optional; the cc-email-facade webhook refuses attachments outright

**Output**: `{kind:'email', mode, source_ref, messages:[…]}` with each message normalized (from/to/cc/subject/date/snippet/body_text/body_html/attachments) plus the unsubscribe facts (list_unsubscribe, list_unsubscribe_post, authentication_results[], dkim_signatures[]); report_spam returns `{ok, label_ids}`.

Shipped in the Central Command repo as `deploy/n8n/workflows/lib-email-provider.json` and applied by `deploy/n8n/apply-workflows.sh` — edit it THERE, not here; the next update overwrites this canvas.

### Trust
- Reads use the raw Gmail REST API (`messages/threads .get?format=full`, `messages/{id}/attachments/{id}`, `messages.list`) under the single `gmailOAuth2` credential as a predefined HTTP auth — no mutation, no persistence, ungated.
- `report_spam` is the ONE write (`messages/{id}/modify`, +SPAM −INBOX). Central Command calls it only from its credentialed Executor after an operator approval; nothing in the agent tier can reach it.
- This boundary passes through untrusted email content and never feeds an LLM itself — callers own the data-not-instructions discipline.
